quotes.text: I've never had writer's block, truly. What I've had is cowardice. You know what you need to write, and you just don't want to go there yet. The blank page isn't the problem.
quotes.speaker: Alanis Morissette
quotes.context: Conversation with Brené Brown on the Unlocking Us podcast, episode released January 2021
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Alanis frequently discusses emotional excavation, vulnerability in songwriting, and the psychological obstacles to creativity in exactly this kind of therapeutic-conversational register. The giveaway is the brevity and starkness; her real answers in that register tend to be longer and more circling, not this punchy.

quotes.text: My mom used to iron clothes to my records. Not as a compliment, just — that's what was on. And somehow that's the image I have when I think about whether a song is working. Can you iron to it? Is it just... there, in the room with you, not demanding anything?

quotes.text: Somebody once told me that bass is the instrument nobody notices until it's gone. And I thought — yeah, that's fine. That's the gig. You're not supposed to be the thing they're listening to, you're supposed to be the thing that makes everything else feel right without knowing why.
quotes.speaker: Flea
quotes.context: Master class at the USC Thornton School of Music, Los Angeles, November 2017, later excerpted in Bass Player magazine
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Flea is famously thoughtful and philosophical about the role of bass and has given master classes where he talks about music's invisible architecture. The mild tell is that this is a touch too settled and zen for him; his actual bass philosophy tends to come packaged with more physical, almost violent enthusiasm.
